title: RBAC v2: Audit ingest lag postmortem
summary: On 2026-01-17 a permissions change related to RBAC v2 rollout removed required permissions from the audit-exporter service account, causing authenticated SIEM ingestion requests to fail and resulting in approximately 6 hours of missing audit events in downstream SIEM dashboards. No production user data was exfiltrated. Detection and recovery were completed within 8 hours; backlog re-ingest was completed over the following 24 hours.
timeline: 2026-01-17 02:10 UTC - RBAC v2 rollout (deploy: rb-2026-01-17) triggered; 02:12 UTC - scheduled change applied to 'platform-service-roles' group; 02:15 UTC - audit-exporter service account lost 'log-ingest' grant due to policy override; 02:18 UTC - SIEM ingest pipeline started returning 401/403 for audit-exporter requests; 02:20 UTC - monitoring alert 'audit-siem-ingest-rate-drop' fired; 02:25 UTC - on-call security engineer (Diego) paged; 03:00 UTC - attempted immediate retry/backpressure handled by exporter but auth failures persisted; 04:45 UTC - RBAC rollback completed to restore 'log-ingest' on service account (PR #6421); 05:10 UTC - SIEM accepted new requests; 05:45 UTC - audit-exporter flushed buffered events; 08:00 UTC - initial verification of event continuity complete; 2026-01-18 11:00 UTC - final backfill completed and verified against S3 raw-audit archives.
detection: Alerting: automated metric-based alert 'audit-siem-ingest-rate-drop' (alerts-team threshold) detected a sustained >70% reduction in event rate. SIEM correlation dashboards (auth-failures view) showed a spike in 401/403 statuses from audit-exporter origin. Pager went to on-call security, who engaged SRE. Initial detection time to page: ~5 minutes.
impact: - ~6 hours of reduced/incomplete audit events visible in SIEM (estimated 120k events).
root_cause: Primary cause: mis-scoped RBAC v2 policy change that inadvertently removed the 'log-ingest' permission from the audit-exporter service account. Contributing causes: 1) change was applied without a targeted canary for service accounts that perform machine-to-machine SIEM ingest, 2) our RBAC CI tests only validate human-role mappings and did not include automated checks for critical service account grants, 3) the audit-exporter lacked robust auth-failure retry/backoff and replay logic for 401/403 failures, 4) monitoring alerted on rate drop but runbook lacked a quick checklist for 'permissions rollback' steps for RBAC changes.
remediation: Immediate: rollback RBAC change to restore 'log-ingest' grant to audit-exporter service account; validate SIEM ingestion and flush buffered events. Short-term: implement CI gating to run a 'service-account permission smoke test' during RBAC policy changes that exercises ingest endpoints with service account creds. Medium-term: extend audit-exporter to queue and retry failed auth responses with exponential backoff and to publish failure metrics to a dedicated 'exporter-auth-errors' metric stream. Update runbooks to include explicit RBAC rollback steps and contact matrix. Long-term: update RBAC change process to include canary scope rules and mandatory 'safety list' of service accounts that cannot lose specific grants without human approval.
postmortem_notes: No indicators of credential compromise were found; authentication failures were purely permission-denied errors (403) caused by policy removal. The audit log schema was unaffected and raw logs remained in S3. Backfill used raw-audit archives to replay into SIEM. During replay we observed minor timestamp skew which required a small normalization pass; that was addressed by a one-off transformation script. Communication: customer-facing statement drafted and reviewed by legal for compliance-facing customers; internal exec summary prepared for CTO and Head of Security.
action_items: SEC-1290: Add service-account permission smoke tests to RBAC CI (owner: Priya Nair, due: 2026-02-05)
INFRA-3344: Add 'exporter-auth-errors' metric and dashboard; correlate with SIEM ingest rate (owner: Marcus Williams, due: 2026-02-01)
SEC-1291: Update RBAC change runbook to require safety-list approval and canary scope; include quick rollback checklist (owner: Aisha Malik, due: 2026-01-31)
EXPORTER-210: Add replay-safe queueing and exponential backoff for 401/403 responses; include idempotent replay key support (owner: Diego Alvarez, due: 2026-03-01)
COMMS-78: Publish incident runbook and customer-facing notification template for audit ingestion incidents (owner: Lena Zhang, due: 2026-02-10)
lessons_learned: 1) RBAC changes must treat critical machine principals differently than human roles; enforce safety lists. 2) CI must include integration smoke tests that exercise high-risk M2M paths. 3) Evidence automation and SIEM ingest should tolerate transient auth failures and provide robust backfill paths. 4) Monitoring alerts are only useful if runbooks include concise triage steps for the likely root causes (permissions vs network vs service).
follow_up_verification: Post-remediation verification steps: run full-week simulated RBAC change in staging with service-account smoke tests (owner: Priya Nair, verify by: 2026-02-07); run two dry-run SIEM replay exercises from raw-audit archives (owner: Diego Alvarez, verify by: 2026-02-14); audit RBAC CI coverage report and confirm 95%+ coverage of service-account critical grants (owner: Security Eng, verify by: 2026-03-01).
